newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria, oil partners yet to agree new profit share.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria, oil partners yet to agree new profit share.

text.p: Negotiations on a revised Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between Nigeria and its joint venture oil partners have been held up over the profit margin the partners should enjoy, a senior oil executive said.

"We are yet to agree on the profit margin allowed the oil firms so the negotiations are still deadlocked," George Kirkland, managing director of Chevron Nigeria, a joint venture between Chevron Corp and state-run NNPC told reporters in Lagos on Tuesday.
The existing MOU which came into effect in 1991 offered the oil firms $2.50 per barrel profit margin.
But the companies say this has been eroded over the years by inflation and various taxes levied on them and have proposed that it be raised to $3 and $5 per barrel.
Negotiations between the two parties on the new MOU started in 1995. They last met in October 1996.
"We are hoping to get the government back to the negotiating table as soon as possible," Kirkland said.

Nigeria produces about two million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil, most of which comes from its joint venture partners namely Shell, Mobil Corp, Chevron Corp, Agip SpA, Texaco Inc and Elf Aquitaine.
The country is targeting a daily production capacity of 2.5 million bpd by 2000 and is trying to encourage the oil firms to increase exploration and production activities through incentives.

"That would depend on the level of funds provided by the government for the joint venture programmes," Kirkland said, adding that the oil firms were anxiously awaiting the 1997 budget to determine their course of action.

The budget, expected to shed light on various issues like possible privatisation of the oil industry, is due to be broadcast by military ruler General Sani Abacha any time from now after the ruling council approved it on Tuesday. --Lagos newsroom +234 1 2630317
